To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the metamaterial mushroom structures can be used as a low-profile and compact solution for mutual coupling reduction of MIMO slot antennas.
the proposed double-layer mushroom structure-loaded fourelement SICBS antenna system can achieve ultra-low interelement mutual coupling over the bandwidth of interest.
a four-element SICBCS antenna system loaded with metamaterial structures can be used for ultra-low inter-element coupling in the frequency range of 2.3-2.5 GHz.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel design of a four-element MIMO SICBS antenna system based on metamaterial structures.

the mutual coupling suppression of compact four-element SICB antenna systems based on metamaterial mushroom structures, which is of great importance for the application of MIMO systems in the 5G wireless communications.
the design of compact four-element SICB slot antenna system with ultra-low inter-element coupling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the double-layer mushroom cells loaded on the top of the SICBS antennas are more effective for the mutual coupling suppression than the double-layer mushroom wall positioned in between the antenna elements, and that the metamaterial mushroom cells can be effectively used for the mutual coupling reduction in the SICBS-based MIMO antenna systems.

a four-element SICB S antenna system with a double-layer metamaterial mushroom structure positioned above the SISCB antenna elements is an effective and compact solution for the mutual coupling suppression of MIMO antenna system in the 2.4 GHz WLAN band.
the proposed metamaterial mushroom structure-loaded compact four-element SICB antenna systems have achieved ultra-low inter-element coupling of -40dB with a bandwidth of 2%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a compact MIMO system can achieve an excellent performance with ultra-low mutual coupling, high gain, and low profile.

the metamaterial-loaded four-element MIMO SICBS antenna system is capable of achieving ultra-low mutual coupling and high isolation between the antenna elements, which is very important for MIMO systems.
, by using the metamaterial mushroom structures, the mutual coupling between the four-element SICSB antenna systems can be effectively reduced and the antenna performance is also improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metamaterials can be used to achieve ultra-low interelement mutual coupling in MIMO antenna systems.

the use of metamaterial structures can be an effective approach to reduce the mutual coupling of compact MIMO antenna systems, which can also be extended for the reduction of mutual coupling between the antenna elements of other MIMO configurations.
the metamaterial structure-loaded MIMO antenna systems can be designed to have ultra-low inter-element coupling and wide impedance bandwidth, which are important for MIMO systems.
